title: Disaster response capability varies sharply across states and localities while federal role changes remain consequential
source_unit: GAO-26-108599, Disaster Assistance High-Risk Series: State and Local Response Capabilities
geography: United States; 10 states receiving major disaster declarations for selected recent disasters, with federal, state, and local institutional evidence

observations.period: Hurricanes Helene and Milton, 2024; Los Angeles wildfires and Texas floods, 2025; report published December 18, 2025

denominator.unit: states with major disaster declarations whose preparedness assessments GAO analyzed

capability_variation.value: state and local disaster-response capability levels varied widely
capability_variation.unit: selected-state preparedness assessments and official interviews

rural_resource_gap.value: rural or less-resourced jurisdictions faced capability challenges even when located within a well-resourced state

federal_support.value: states and localities rely substantially on federal grants, training, technical assistance, and response support

transition_requirements.value: officials emphasized clear guidance, time to prepare, and continued federal coordination when disaster roles change

catastrophic_floor.value: federal officials said even the best-equipped states would require some federal financial or other support for catastrophic disasters

observations.method: GAO analyzed preparedness assessments for 10 states, summarized selected FEMA preparedness-grant and disaster-response assistance data, and reviewed interviews with federal, state, and local officials.
observations.uncertainty: The selected states, disasters, assessments, and interviews are not a representative estimate of national capability. The report does not measure response speed, survivor receipt, repair, health, housing, local economic recovery, or the causal effect of any federal-role change.
observations.subgroup: Federal agencies, selected state and local governments, rural and less-resourced jurisdictions, and jurisdictions affected by the selected recent disasters; these are institutional units rather than a survivor panel.
observations.counterinterpretation: Variation in capability may reflect different hazards, responsibilities, local choices, or measurement practices rather than a single national decline; federal pooling can also be an efficient complement to local capacity rather than evidence of local failure.

related_sources.claim: Accessible report provides the preparedness-assessment, interview, and intergovernmental-role context.
Related FEMA survivor-assistance evidence; institutional response capability and survivor-level receipt remain separate stages.

boundary: This record adds a selected-jurisdiction capability and federal-dependence layer. It does not establish a national capability rate, survivor-level access or outcome, local economic recovery, public trust, or political action.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official GAO landing page and accessible report reviewed; underlying assessments, administrative data, and interview materials are not retained.
